title: introduce-client-declare-header-and-v2-compatibility-shim-for-tool-calls-and-streaming
author: Ava Kaplan
release_notes: Add X-Redwood-Client-Schema header to let clients opt into schema versions; add server-side shim to gracefully backfill v1->v2 structured output + tool-call envelopes. No user-facing breaking changes; opt-in beta header for new clients.
description:
Summary: Adds a lightweight compatibility shim and opt-in client header so older clients can continue to call the new schema-v2 API surface without breaking streaming, tool/function call envelopes, or structured outputs. This PR introduces the 'X-Redwood-Client-Schema' request header (values: v1, v2, auto) used by the API gateway/runtime to choose transformation rules. When header is absent, behavior defaults to 'auto' which preserves existing semantics. Motivation: customers reported flaky tool-call envelopes and truncated streaming behavior after schema changes rolled out to v2. Instead of a hard rollback, we need a short-lived server-side translator that preserves correctness while clients migrate. Context: relates to ENG-1203 (schema rollout plan), PM-409 (customer compatibility requests), and a support ticket SUP-872 from a partner integrator experiencing nested tool outputs being dropped during chunked streaming. This PR is intended as a backward-compat shim for the next 8-12 weeks while we pursue client upgrades and a broader schema negotiation handshake.

What changed (high level):
- API gateway: accept and validate new header 'X-Redwood-Client-Schema', expose parsed client_capabilities to request context.
- Compatibility shim: server-side middleware that performs: 1) stream envelope normalization (ensures incremental chunks contain complete token envelopes for tool calls), 2) v2->v1 structured output coercion (maps optional typed fields to legacy text-first fallback), 3) sanitized event ordering for partial tool call events to prevent premature 'end' semantics.
- Tool/function calling layer: added logic to attach canonical 'tool_call' sentinel metadata to streaming delta events so legacy clients see ordered tool call lifecycle (start/args/complete) instead of collapsed final payload only.
- Tests: added integration tests that simulate chunked streams from runtime and assert legacy client reassembly of tool call envelopes. End-to-end tests exercise both header variants (v1, v2, auto).
- Telemetry: emit 'compat_shim_applied' and 'client_schema_header' tags to trace logs and metrics for rollout monitoring.

Commits (summary):
- 3f1b9a8: add header parsing + request context plumbing
- 7b6d2c3: implement shim: stream normalizer + v2->v1 mapper
- 9a84f11: add unit tests for mapper and stream normalizer
- a2cbe55: hook compat shim into tool-calling runtime path and add feature flag
- d41f02e: add integration tests and qa harness scripts
- e9b7c44: update docs + migration note in api.md

Files changed (high level):
- api/gateway/headers.go (new header parsing and validation)
- runtime/compat/shim.go (core translation logic)
- runtime/compat/mapper_test.go (unit tests)
- runtime/tooling/stream_emitter.go (ordered tool-call metadata)
- docs/api/migration.md (migration guide + example curl)

- ci/flows/compat-smoke.yaml (new smoke test job)

Review conversation (selected):
- Diego Martinez (reviewer): "This looks good overall — I like the approach of opt-in header + auto fallback. Two asks: (1) can we make the shim idempotent if it sees partially-coalesced tool events? (2) add a metric for shim-invocations where we also tag whether we performed coercion or not." 
  - Author (Ava): "Agree on both. Implemented idempotency (shim now checks for canonical sentinels) and added 'compat_shim_action' metric with values 'noop'|'coerce'|'normalize'."
- Priya Shah: "Minor: please ensure telemetry doesn't include PII. Also ensure the migration docs show how to set header in SDKs (python/ts)." 
  - Author: "Stripped user text from emitted telemetry; added SDK snippets in docs." 
- Ethan Cole: "CI flake observed in e2e streaming test — intermittent ordering mismatch on low-latency mode. I see you added a 5ms debounce; is that safe for low-latency SLOs?" 
  - Author: "Adjusted debounce to be adaptive: only used when the emitter detects out-of-order chunk metadata. Added benchmark notes and feature flag to disable in specific Dedicated pools." 
- Approvals: Diego approved after follow-ups; Priya approved; Ethan approved once debounce made adaptive. Final reviewer comment: "Approved — good incremental approach. Monitor compat_shim_applied metric and alert if >5% of traffic after 2 weeks."

CI summary: 
- Unit tests: pass
- Integration tests: initially failed (ordering race), rerun after debounce fix: pass
- Lint/format: pass
- Compatibility smoke job (ci/flows/compat-smoke.yaml): pass on second run
- Overall: pass

QA and rollout plan: 
- Feature-flagged rollout behind 'compat_shim' flag. Default enabled in hosted API for 2 weeks, disabled for Dedicated by default. Gradual ramp by percent-of-traffic (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with monitoring alerts.
- Telemetry dashboard: new panel for 'compat_shim_applied' broken down by header value and 'compat_shim_action'. Alert if errors related to tool_call lifecycle increase > 10% or if shim application exceeds 8% of requests in 'auto' mode (indicates many legacy clients still not upgraded).
- Post-merge migration note: set SDKs to emit 'X-Redwood-Client-Schema: v2' when they consume typed structured outputs and tool-calls; sample code added to docs.

Backward-compat guarantees and limits: 
- Guarantee: legacy clients will not see protocol-level terminations or truncated tool payloads as a result of this server-side shim. The shim only rewrites streaming envelopes and structured fields for HTTP/WS streaming and does not modify model outputs.
- Limitations: not a substitute for clients that rely on very specific token boundaries for deterministic parsing; recommend those clients add explicit markers or migrate to header-based negotiation.

Related docs/notes: docs/api/migration.md includes examples for Python/TS SDK header insertion and manual curl examples for testing streaming behavior. Also added a troubleshooting section for 'partial-tool-call' symptoms and how to toggle the shim in Dedicated/private installs.

Follow-ups (post-merge):
- ENG-1203.2: Bake header negotiation into SDK handshake (next sprint).
- ENG-1203.3: Replace shim with a negotiated protocol once >= 95% of clients use v2 header.
- PM-409: Communicate migration window and schedule with partner integrators.

Merge: Squash-merged into main after approvals and CI green. Rollout controlled by feature flag and percent-based ramp. Monitoring and follow-ups owned by Runtime team (Ethan/Diego).
